source_title: Artificial intelligence: Council and Parliament agree to simplify and streamline rules
summary: The follow-up political trilogue on the Digital Omnibus on AI succeeded on 7 May 2026, reaching a provisional agreement between the Council and the European Parliament after the 28-29 April round had ended without agreement. The agreement defers the application of obligations for standalone high-risk AI systems under Annex III from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, and for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I to 2 August 2028. It also introduces new prohibitions (non-consensual intimate deepfakes / CSAM) applying from 2 December 2026 and moves the Article 50(2) synthetic-content marking transition to 2 December 2026. The provisional agreement was approved by Member States' ambassadors (Coreper) on 13 May 2026.
mechanical_change: Still a proposal at this stage: the provisional agreement changes no AI Act text until it is formally adopted by both institutions and published in the Official Journal. Original deadlines (including 2 August 2026 for Annex III) remained legally binding as at this date.
verified_by: Council of the EU press release (7 May 2026); European Parliament press release 20260427IPR42011; corroborated by White & Case, Inside Privacy, IAPP
